subject.name_or_desc: A clergyman (the querent, described by Lilly as covetous, of good wit and volubility of tongue) seeking a benefice

context.question: If he should obtain the parsonage (benefice) desired?
context.setting: He had lately lost the benefit of some good place in the Commonwealth and was solicitous how to live in his former credit; he pressed his suit for the parsonage despite Lilly's advice

attachments.key_positions: Saturn impedited in the Ascendant, 'infortuning' the question; Jupiter lord of the 9th (significator of the benefice) in no aspect with Mars(?) lord of the Ascendant, nor the Moon in any aspect with him; neither lord of the Ascendant nor Moon placed in the 9th; no translation or collection of light, and no reception between the significators; Moon separating from a trine and applying to an opposition of Mercury, lord of the 3rd; Venus in the 7th house opposing the Ascendant
attachments.note: Some planet glyphs are garbled in the 1647 OCR; the seven numbered negative testimonies are Lilly's own enumeration.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
